output: Scientific Hypothesis: In the context of the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79) dataset, time preference, as measured by savings behavior (DISSAVED and SAMESAVE), does not significantly impact BMI in Hispanic men. This hypothesis is based on the analysis of the dataset, where the variables DISSAVED and SAMESAVE were used as indicators of time preference, and BMI was the dependent variable. The correlation analysis and regression results showed very weak and statistically insignificant relationships between these variables, suggesting that time preference does not have a significant impact on BMI in this population.
